title: 1d7suu
Siffin, the Arbitration and Martyrdom
hook: At Siffin the mushafs were hung on spears; Imam Ali patiently spoke the truth, and his caliphate ended in martyrdom at a dawn prayer.
scenes.0.text: When the Camel ended, **Imam Ali** made Kufa his center. From there he marched to Syria. On the banks of the Euphrates, at **Siffin**, **Mu'awiya**'s army came out against him. **Imam Ali** avoided starting the fighting himself. The one in the right was **Imam Ali**. He was not the side that drew the sword first.
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.0.art.actors.2.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.1.text: The Syrian army, holding the bank of the Euphrates, did not let **Imam Ali**'s soldiers go down to the water. Imam Ali sent **Sa'sa'a b. Suhan** to Mu'awiya and asked him, before any talk of war, to stand aside from between the people and the water. In Mu'awiya's council **al-Walid b. Uqba** shouted, "Kill them with thirst," and Mu'awiya sent his horsemen to guard the water. Imam Ali's soldiers remained without water for a day and a night. In the end they drew their swords, advanced on the Syrian ranks and took the bank of the Euphrates from them. This time it was the Syrian side that fell into fear, and **Amr b. al-As** asked Mu'awiya what would happen if they did to him today what he had done to them yesterday. When Mu'awiya said, "What do you think of Ali?", Amr gave this answer: "I think he will not permit against you what you permitted against him." Imam Ali's soldiers, who had tasted thirst, were saying, "By God, we will not give them a single drop." According to the narrations, Imam Ali told them, "No, by God, I will not repay them with the like of what they did," and sent this order: "Take as much water as you need and return to your camp. Stand aside from between them and the water. God has given you victory because of their injustice and transgression." Those who had cut off the water only yesterday filled their vessels from the same bank, and the horses of both armies drank from the same water. Imam Ali's honesty was such that even the enemy who drew a sword against him trusted his character.
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.1.art.actors.2.label: pt51vl
Amr b. al-As
scenes.2.text: Years earlier, while the mosque was being built, the Prophet was beside **Ammar**. Looking at him he had said, "Woe to Ammar, a rebellious group will kill him." The Companions heard this saying. Baghi means one who fights against the legitimate imam. This saying would show who the baghi was at Siffin.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.2.art.actors.1.label: sf7oxz
Ammar b. Yasir
scenes.3.text: At **Siffin**, the aged **Ammar** was martyred in **Imam Ali**'s ranks. The Prophet had said that ==a baghi group== would kill him. That group was **Mu'awiya**'s army. Those who love him saw that day that the Prophet's report was fulfilled on **Mu'awiya**'s side.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: sf7oxz
Ammar b. Yasir
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.4.text: At **Siffin**, **Amr b. al-As** reminded **Mu'awiya** of the hadith, saying "We have killed Ammar." **Mu'awiya** said, "Did we kill him? Those who brought him killed him." He cast the blame on those who brought Ammar there. The Prophet's report was clear. ==The baghi group== twisted the saying in order to deny this report.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: pt51vl
Amr b. al-As
scenes.4.art.actors.1.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.5.text: At **Siffin**, as the battle was turning in **Imam Ali**'s favor, the Syrians fixed a mushaf on a spear. They said, "Let God's Book be the arbiter between us." This was not worship, it was ==a trick.== **Imam Ali** said at that moment that it was a trick. Part of his army stopped him, saying the Quran was on the spear. While the side in the right had the upper hand, the battle was cut short.
scenes.5.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.6.text: At **Siffin** an agreement was written. Hakam means a judge chosen by the parties. **Imam Ali** had asked for other names. Even so, Abu Musa and **Amr b. al-As** sat. The title "Commander of the Faithful" was removed from the text. This arbitration weakened the authority proclaimed at Ghadir. It harmed **Imam Ali**'s right.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: 8bxja1
Abu Musa al-Ash'ari
scenes.6.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.6.art.actors.2.label: pt51vl
Amr b. al-As
scenes.7.text: A group from **Imam Ali**'s army rejected the arbitration. Saying "Judgment belongs to God alone," they left his side. These are called the Kharijites. Imam Ali said, "The word is true, but falsehood is intended by it." First they were spoken with. Then there was fighting at Nahrawan. The trick of the mushaf on the spear had split **Imam Ali**'s own ranks as well.
scenes.7.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.8.text: **Imam Ali** relates a report from the Prophet about the Kharijites. Those who kill them have a reward with God. The side closer to the truth will fight them. That side is Imam Ali's ranks.
scenes.8.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.9.text: After Siffin, **Mu'awiya** ordered that **Imam Ali** be ==cursed== and reviled from the pulpits under his rule. At the head of the advice he gave to **al-Mughira b. Shu'ba**, whom he sent to Kufa as governor, was that he should not hold back from reviling and disparaging Imam Ali. In the Friday sermons the Prophet's legatee and son-in-law was being disparaged. One day Mu'awiya asked the Companion **Sa'd b. Abi Waqqas** why he did not revile Abu Turab, that is, Imam Ali. Sa'd listed three things the Prophet had said about Imam Ali: the hadith of Manzila, the banner of Khaybar and the day of Mubahala. For this reason, he said, he would never revile him. This injustice continued until years later the Umayyad caliph **Umar b. Abd al-Aziz** forbade it. Umar b. Abd al-Aziz ordered that, in place of the curse, the 90th verse of Surat al-Nahl be recited in the sermons.
scenes.9.art.actors.0.label: 17k143j
Sa'd b. Abi Waqqas
scenes.9.art.actors.1.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.10.text: In the 40th year of the Hijra, in the month of Ramadan, the dawn prayer was being performed in the great mosque of Kufa. While **Imam Ali** was leading the prayer, **Ibn Muljam** of the Kharijites struck his blessed head with a sword he had steeped in poison for a whole month. Imam Ali fell inside the mihrab. According to the narrations, at that moment he said, "By the Lord of the Kaaba, I have triumphed." He was carried home wounded. He bore no grudge against his killer. He asked that he be given food and water and be treated well during his captivity. He left the bequest that, if he died, only one blow be struck for one blow and that the killer's limbs not be cut off. At the end of his caliphate, which lasted about four years and nine months, he left his bequest to his son **Imam Hasan**. The imam whose hand the Prophet had raised at Ghadir was martyred in the mihrab.
scenes.10.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.10.art.actors.1.label: 1bj9fo
Imam Hasan
sunni.0.says: During the building of the mosque the Prophet says about Ammar, "A rebellious group will kill him." In some copies the addition "they call him to the Fire" is absent; there is a note by al-Humaydi and Ibn Hajar on this.
sunni.1.says: The hadith about Ammar, "A rebellious group will kill him."
sunni.1.grade: Sahih; since it occurs in Bukhari and Muslim, at the level of muttafaq alayh
sunni.2.says: The report of the Ammar hadith in the Musnad; the Dar al-Salam note states that it is sahih and that it coincides with Muslim 2915.
sunni.3.says: Amr b. al-As's reminding Mu'awiya of the hadith and Mu'awiya's reply "Those who brought him killed him."
sunni.4.says: Imam Ali relates from the Prophet the report about the Kharijite community; they recite their Qurans and this is evidence against them; Imam Ali says "the word is true, but falsehood is intended by it."
sunni.5.says: The report that the one of the two parties closer to the truth will kill the community that will depart from the religion. Commentators such as al-Nawawi understand this expression as Imam Ali's side (details to be checked).
sunni.6.says: Mu'awiya says to Sa'd b. Abi Waqqas, "Why do you not revile Abu Turab?" Sa'd lists three sayings of the Prophet about Imam Ali (the Manzila, the banner of Khaybar, the Mubahala) and says he would not agree to this. The wording is open to two readings: "why do you not revile" and "what prevented you."
sunni.7.says: The report "Ali is with the Quran, and the Quran is with Ali" (Umm Salama). Al-Hakim says the chain is sahih; in the Adil Murshid edition a note of "very weak" is added because of Abu Sa'id al-Taymi and Abu Thabit.
sunni.7.grade: Disputed: al-Hakim says sahih, some muhaddiths find it weak
sunni.8.says: Siffin, the hanging of mushafs on spears, the Arbitration, Nahrawan, Ibn Muljam and the tradition of reviling in the Umayyad period (the period of al-Mughira b. Shu'ba, the incident of Hujr b. Adi).
sunni.9.says: The course of events and the practice of reviling Imam Ali.
sunni.10.says: That Umar b. Abd al-Aziz abolished the tradition of cursing Imam Ali; that verse Nahl 90 was had recited in the sermons is conveyed as a widespread account.
sunni.11.says: The report that the Prophet told Imam Ali that the most wretched of those after him would kill him.
sunni.12.says: Most Ahl al-Sunna scholars find Imam Ali closer to the truth; they accept that the Ammar hadith points to Mu'awiya's group and count them as being in an error of ijtihad. Ibn Taymiyya does not call Imam Ali wrong but thinks the war was not commanded. None of these reports has been verified from a primary text.
sunni.13.says: The view that Imam Ali's imamate is the truth is attributed to him. Unverified report.
sunni.14.says: Imam Ali sends Sa'sa'a b. Suhan to Mu'awiya asking him to stand aside from between the people and the water. Al-Walid b. Uqba says "Kill them with thirst"; Amr b. al-As advises opening the water. Mu'awiya sends horsemen to hold the water. Imam Ali's soldiers take the water and say "We will not let them drink." Imam Ali sends word: "Take what you need, return to your camp and leave them to the water; God has given you victory because of their injustice and transgression." The report is through Abu Mikhnaf.
sunni.14.grade: Historical report (Abu Mikhnaf). The episode also appears in Sunni historians such as Ibn al-Athir and Ibn al-Jawzi.
sunni.15.says: When Imam Ali's soldiers seize the water they say "By God, we will not let the Syrians drink"; Imam Ali sends word: "Take what you need and leave them; God has given you victory because of their transgression and injustice."
sunni.16.says: In the year 41, appointing al-Mughira b. Shu'ba governor of Kufa, Mu'awiya advises him: "Do not hold back from reviling and disparaging Ali; ask mercy for Uthman; find fault with Ali's companions and keep them away."
sunni.17.says: After the blow, speaking to Umm Kulthum, Ibn Muljam says "By God, I poisoned it for a month"; the narrator explains that he means his sword. Imam Ali also asks that the captive be treated well, his bed and food kept good.
shia.0.says: The course of Siffin, Ammar's martyrdom, the text of the agreement and the debates over the choice of arbiters. In Sunni rijal criticism Nasr is counted as an "extreme Shia," but in terms of material he is an early source.
shia.1.says: Imam Ali's speeches concerning Siffin and the Kharijites. There is debate over the attribution of the sermons.
shia.2.says: A detailed account of Imam Ali's martyrdom and his bequests.
shia.3.says: The general course of events. He is considered a historian with Shia leanings.
shia.4.says: The claim that the sabb tradition lasted about sixty years, and Umar b. Abd al-Aziz's prohibition of it, attributed to Ibn Khaldun. It is a secondary source.
shia.5.says: P.162: Mu'awiya tells Abu al-A'war "Keep them from the water"; Imam Ali's soldiers take the water by fighting and say "We will not let them drink"; Imam Ali sends word: "Take what you need, return to your camp and stand aside from between them and the water; God has given you victory because of their transgression and injustice." P.185: the water-skins and horses of both armies are described drinking from the same water. P.186: Amr b. al-As tells Mu'awiya, "Ali will not permit against you what you permitted against him."
shia.5.grade: Early historical source. In Sunni rijal criticism Nasr is regarded as an "extreme Shi'i".
shia.6.says: When Imam Ali seizes the water his soldiers say "Keep them from the water, kill them with thirst"; Imam Ali answers: "No, by God, I will not repay them with the like of what they did. Open part of the watering place to them; the edge of the sword makes that unnecessary." The commentator is a Mu'tazili scholar.
shia.6.grade: Late commentary (7th/13th century); the general frame of the episode agrees with the early sources.
disputes.0.title: kck4nn
Whom does the rebellious group point to?
disputes.0.sunni: That Ammar was martyred at Siffin in Imam Ali's ranks is common ground in the sources. The Sunni majority regards the hadith as pointing to Mu'awiya's group and understands this as an error of ijtihad.
disputes.0.shia: That Ammar was martyred at Siffin in Imam Ali's ranks is common ground in the sources. In the Shia account, this shows that Mu'awiya's side was in the wrong.
disputes.1.title: 4oq63w
Is Muslim 2404 a command or a question?
disputes.1.sunni: It is written in Muslim that Mu'awiya asked Sa'd a question about Imam Ali. Some commentators read this as a question, not a command.
disputes.1.shia: It is written in Muslim that Mu'awiya asked Sa'd a question about Imam Ali. In the Shia account, this is regarded as evidence that reviling was widespread in that period.
disputes.2.title: 1e61uu8
Was Abu Musa deceived at the Arbitration?
disputes.2.sunni: The arbitration meeting is narrated in both traditions. Modern historians look with caution at the details of the scene in which Amr deceived Abu Musa.
disputes.2.shia: The arbitration meeting is narrated in both traditions. Classical accounts report that Amr deceived Abu Musa; the decision itself is also disputed.
disputes.3.title: 13lgnpl
Ibn Muljam and the day of his death
disputes.3.sunni: It is narrated that Ibn Muljam wounded Imam Ali at the dawn prayer. The day of death is reported as 17, 19 or 21 Ramadan; the three-assassination plan is received with caution.
disputes.3.shia: It is narrated that Ibn Muljam wounded Imam Ali at the dawn prayer. In the Shia tradition the day of death is given as 21 Ramadan.
questions.0: The Prophet had foretold that a rebellious group would kill Ammar. At Siffin, Ammar was with Imam Ali. How does this report make you think about standing with the Ahl al-Bayt?
questions.1: When Ammar was martyred, the hadith was recalled and was met with "Those who brought him killed him." What does the distance between a report and its interpretation tell you?
questions.2: When asked, Sa'd listed three sayings of the Prophet about Imam Ali. How do these sayings describe to you the love felt for him?
questions.3: Umar b. Abd al-Aziz abolished the practice of reviling Imam Ali from the pulpits. How does this step show you the weight of those words?
questions.4: The Prophet had foretold that, concerning the Kharijites, the side closer to the truth would fight them. Imam Ali met them. How does this report let you read his place?
summary: At Siffin, Ammar was martyred in Imam Ali's ranks. The mushafs were hung on spears; the Arbitration and Nahrawan followed. Imam Ali patiently kept his right and was martyred at a dawn prayer.
key: Siffin, the mushafs and the arbitration
notes.0: At Siffin the armies of Imam Ali and Mu'awiya met.
notes.1: Ammar b. Yasir was martyred in Imam Ali's ranks; the hadith «a rebellious group will kill him» was recalled.
notes.2: The Syrians tied mushafs to spears and demanded arbitration.
notes.3: The group that rejected the arbitration split off; these are called the Kharijites.
notes.4: Ibn Muljam wounded Imam Ali in Ramadan 40; Imam Ali passed away about two days later.
